notes.text: Enron Office of the Chairman (Ken) announced that on 2002-01-03 Enron settled a procedural dispute with Dynegy over Northern Natural Gas, allowing Dynegy to exercise its option to acquire the pipeline and dismissing Dynegy's Texas lawsuit.
Under the Dynegy settlement, Enron's right to repurchase Northern Natural Gas was extended until June 30.
Ken said the settlement lets Enron pursue its $10 billion damage claim against Dynegy and avoid costly litigation in state courts; the settlement is part of Enron's efforts to come out of bankruptcy.
Ken said Enron still has some 9,000 miles of safe, profitable interstate pipelines as a base to rebuild its core businesses after Northern Natural Gas.
Stan Horton told ETS employees that Dynegy will assume interim control of Northern Natural Gas, Enron will not contest interim possession, and ETS will work on a smooth transition.
